# Tln — the modern expert-system language

> Tln modernizes Prolog (ISO/IEC 13211-1:1995) expert systems into a deterministic, testable,
> data-native rule platform. A native Go engine (lexer → parser → validator → planner → executor)
> evaluates readable rule blocks over a pluggable FactStore. Facts are loaded from external systems
> as entity–attribute triples — record(Entity, Id, Type, Category, Status, Date) and
> attr(Entity, Id, Name, Value) — never written in .tln. Rules read like English. Core blocks:
> define, rule (allow/block), detect, recommend, combine. Built-in ML: predict (CART), classify
> (kNN), forecast (exp smoothing), cluster (DBSCAN), find similar (cosine), anomaly (z-score/Grubbs),
> learned thresholds, PPR — 11 explainable primitives. Tool orchestration via the plugin-neutral
> `tool "server" "name" {…}` verb (workflow, on-change, collect, enrich), plus a `.tln.test`
> framework and compile-time metaprogramming (defmacro/quote/unquote). Plugin architecture: a
> transport-free core plus SPIs — tools (tln-mcp), I/O (tln-io), storage (tln-db), ASP/stable-model
> solver (tln-asp), and a pure-Go Prolog runtime for porting (tln-prolog). In production it is the
> deterministic decision core of OpenTalon, the
> enterprise AI-orchestration ecosystem (Expert-in-the-Loop: the LLM handles intent, Tln handles
> knowledge and inference).

## Docs
- [Getting Started](https://tln-lang.org/docs/getting-started/): Hello World and the family-tree/ancestor classic side-by-side with Prolog; the mental model (facts as record/attr triples loaded externally vs rules; native-Go planner + FactStore; Expert-in-the-Loop); and the CLI (tln build/test/run/explain/repl).
- [Language Reference](https://tln-lang.org/docs/reference/): core blocks (define, rule, detect, recommend, combine), values, operators, selectors (`for records where …`), templates, and priorities.

## Prolog → Tln (side-by-side comparisons; ISO Prolog left, Tln right)
- [Overview + family tree](https://tln-lang.org/comparisons/): the migration thesis; parent/grandparent/ancestor in Prolog vs a Tln detect over record/attr facts; note that existing Prolog can be ported (relational subset → Tln rules; the rest runs on tln-prolog).
- [Insurance claims](https://tln-lang.org/comparisons/insurance-claims/): block/allow rules and cap detection; declarative flag/label vs Prolog query-and-print plumbing.
- [Derived predicates & recursion](https://tln-lang.org/comparisons/reasoning-recursion/): derive/detect chains; negation-through-recursion under well-founded semantics where ISO Prolog's SLDNF loops.
- [Fleet maintenance](https://tln-lang.org/comparisons/fleet-maintenance/): define/detect service intervals, and a forecast Prolog can't express.

## Beyond Prolog
- [MCP tools & workflows](https://tln-lang.org/beyond-prolog/mcp-workflows/): transport-free core returns tool calls as data; reactive on-change → workflow, scheduled collect, enrich, remediate; resolver plugin tln-mcp. Prolog has no native tool I/O.
- [Built-in ML](https://tln-lang.org/beyond-prolog/ml/): predict/classify/forecast/cluster/find and the 11 explainable primitives.
- [Testing](https://tln-lang.org/beyond-prolog/testing/): the .tln.test framework — given / when / expect.

## Plugins (transport-free core; every IO edge is a plugin)
- [Plugins overview](https://tln-lang.org/plugins/): a mod.tln manifest bundles plugins Bundler-style (tln init/bundle/run, no Go host); the plugin-neutral `tool` verb; tools (tln-mcp), I/O (tln-io), storage (tln-db), solver/ASP (tln-asp), Prolog runtime (tln-prolog); the core is a pure language + planner + SPIs.
- [Tln DB](https://tln-lang.org/db/): Go-native embedded fact store + query engine (bbolt + roaring-bitmap index + HNSW vectors) behind the FactStore interface; library or gRPC/HTTP sidecar.

## Agents & workflows
- [Workflows & agents](https://tln-lang.org/workflows/): deterministic agents — the LLM authors a Tln automation once (probabilistic), the runtime runs it every tick with no model in the loop (deterministic). `on` triggers fire `workflow` blocks whose steps call tools; hosted by opentalon-agents. Based on the Deterministic-Where-It-Matters article.

## Production
- [OpenTalon](https://tln-lang.org/opentalon/): the enterprise AI-orchestration system running on Tln; the LLM emits Tln scenarios in a restricted DSL, experts author Tln rules, every IO edge is an isolated plugin.
